title: Palo Alto Networks Certified Prisma Cloud Security Engineer (PCCSE)

nodes.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Microsoft Defender for Cloud (formerly Security Center + Azure Defender) is a Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) and Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) for Azure, multi-cloud, and hybrid environments.

flashcards.front: CSPM vs CWPP — what does each do in Defender for Cloud?
flashcards.back: CSPM: continuously assesses security posture, assigns a Secure Score, and recommends remediations. CWPP: detects and responds to active threats on workloads (VMs, containers, DBs).

flashcards.front: Secure Score — what does it measure?
flashcards.back: A percentage representing how many of Defender's security recommendations you have implemented. Higher = better posture. Each recommendation has a point value.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint vs Defender for Cloud?
flashcards.back: Defender for Endpoint: EDR agent for individual Windows/Linux devices. Defender for Cloud: posture management and threat protection for cloud infrastructure.

flashcards.front: Defender for Cloud coverage beyond Azure?
flashcards.back: Supports AWS and GCP workloads via multicloud connectors, and on-premises servers via Azure Arc — providing a unified security view across environments.

questions.q: A security team wants to continuously detect misconfigured cloud resources—such as publicly readable S3 buckets and security groups open to 0.0.0.0/0—across their AWS, Azure, and GCP accounts. Which Prisma Cloud capability addresses this requirement?
choices: Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM)
Cloud Workload Protection (CWP) with Defenders
Web Application and API Security (WAAS)
Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM)
questions.explanation: CSPM continuously evaluates cloud resource configurations against policies and compliance standards, flagging misconfigurations such as public buckets and overly permissive security groups. CWP protects running workloads (hosts, containers, serverless) through Defenders; WAAS provides Layer 7 application and API protection; CIEM analyzes IAM entitlements—none of which is configuration posture monitoring.

questions.q: To protect every node in a Kubernetes cluster with container runtime defense, vulnerability scanning, and network visibility, how is the Prisma Cloud Container Defender typically deployed?
choices: As a single Deployment with one replica behind a Service
As a DaemonSet so one Defender runs on each cluster node
As a sidecar container injected into every application pod
As a CronJob that scans the cluster on a fixed schedule
questions.explanation: Cluster Container Defenders are deployed as a DaemonSet, guaranteeing one Defender pod per node so runtime protection, vulnerability/compliance scanning, and network visibility cover the entire cluster. A single Deployment or CronJob would not protect every node continuously, and the sidecar approach is the App-Embedded Defender used only where a DaemonSet cannot run (for example, Fargate).

questions.q: An analyst needs to find all AWS EC2 security groups that allow unrestricted inbound SSH (port 22) from the internet. Which Prisma Cloud query approach should they use?
choices: A KQL query run against an Azure Log Analytics workspace
An SPL search in the Splunk investigate console
An RQL config query (config from cloud.resource where ...)
An RQL network query (network from vpc.flow_record where ...)
questions.explanation: Resource Query Language (RQL) config queries inspect resource configuration metadata—'config from cloud.resource where ...'—which is how you identify security groups exposing port 22 to the internet. Network queries analyze VPC flow records of actual traffic, not configuration; KQL and SPL belong to Azure Monitor and Splunk respectively, not Prisma Cloud.

questions.q: When onboarding an AWS account into Prisma Cloud for read-only posture monitoring with a cross-account IAM role, which mechanism establishes trust so that only Prisma Cloud can assume that role?
choices: An IAM user access key and secret stored in Prisma Cloud
A resource-based bucket policy on the CloudTrail S3 bucket
A VPC peering connection to the Prisma Cloud tenant
An external ID configured in the role's trust policy
questions.explanation: Prisma Cloud uses an IAM role whose trust policy grants the Prisma Cloud AWS account sts:AssumeRole, scoped by a unique external ID to prevent the confused-deputy problem. Long-lived access keys are discouraged for ongoing monitoring, and neither a CloudTrail bucket policy nor VPC peering has any role in establishing the assume-role trust.

nodes.title: Compliance frameworks: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Compliance is the discipline of mapping your controls to an external framework (PCI, HIPAA, SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001) and proving it to an auditor. Most exam questions test which framework owns which scope, not the minutiae of each clause.

flashcards.back: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard. Applies to anyone who stores, processes, or transmits cardholder data (PAN, expiry, CVV). 12 high-level requirements: firewalls, no defaults, encrypted storage, encrypted transmission, antivirus, secure dev, restrict access, MFA, log, test, policy. Required by Visa/Mastercard, not by law.

flashcards.front: HIPAA vs HITRUST — what's the difference?
flashcards.back: HIPAA is U.S. law for protected health information (PHI) — sets the legal requirements but is high-level on technical controls. HITRUST CSF is a certifiable framework that operationalizes HIPAA (plus ISO, NIST, PCI) into specific testable controls. Healthcare orgs are legally HIPAA-bound; many also pursue HITRUST cert to prove diligence.

American Institute of CPAs report on a SaaS company's controls across five trust criteria: security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, privacy. Type I = controls designed at a point in time. Type II = controls operated effectively over 6-12 months. Enterprise customers ask for the Type II as proof you're not making it up.

flashcards.front: GDPR — what does it require beyond US-style privacy laws?
flashcards.back: European General Data Protection Regulation. Requires explicit consent (not pre-ticked), right to access / deletion / portability, 72-hour breach notification, data protection officer (for large processors), data minimization, and Privacy Impact Assessments for high-risk processing. Fines: up to 4% of global revenue. Applies to anyone processing EU residents' data, regardless of company location.

questions.q: Your organization must report against an internal security baseline that does not match any built-in framework such as CIS or PCI DSS. What is the appropriate Prisma Cloud approach?
choices: Create a custom compliance standard and map policies to its requirements
Disable all built-in standards and rename CIS to the internal baseline
Export raw RQL results and track the baseline only in a spreadsheet
Open a support ticket so Palo Alto adds the baseline to the catalog
questions.explanation: Prisma Cloud lets you build a custom compliance standard with your own sections and requirements, then map existing or custom policies to it, producing live compliance dashboards and reports. Repurposing CIS is not meaningful, spreadsheets lose continuous monitoring, and you do not need Palo Alto to publish a private internal baseline.

questions.q: How does Prisma Cloud Compute primarily build runtime protection for containers so it can flag anomalous process, network, or filesystem activity?
choices: It requires administrators to hand-write a seccomp profile for every image
It automatically learns per-image behavioral models during a learning period
It blocks all system calls that are not on a static global allowlist by default
It relies solely on CVE signatures pulled from the vulnerability feed
questions.explanation: Prisma Cloud builds runtime models by observing each container image's behavior during an automatic learning period, baselining expected processes, networking, and filesystem activity; deviations from the model raise runtime incidents. It does not require hand-written seccomp profiles, does not ship a blanket syscall denylist by default, and runtime defense is behavioral—distinct from CVE signature scanning.

questions.q: A team wants to fail a Jenkins build when a container image contains critical vulnerabilities, before the image is pushed to the registry. Which Prisma Cloud tool fits in the pipeline?
choices: A Defender DaemonSet running in the production cluster
The CSPM agentless scanner attached to the cloud account
twistcli (or the Jenkins plugin) to scan the image during the build
WAAS rules attached to the application load balancer
questions.explanation: twistcli, and the equivalent CI plugins such as the Jenkins plugin, scan images during the build stage and can fail the build against vulnerability or compliance thresholds—shifting security left before the registry push. Production DaemonSet Defenders, CSPM agentless scanning, and WAAS all act after build or at runtime, not as a pipeline gate.

questions.q: Which Prisma Cloud capability provides Layer 7 protection—OWASP Top 10 mitigation, API security, and bot defense—for web applications running on containers or hosts?
choices: CNNF (Cloud Native Network Firewall)
CIEM (Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management)
CSPM data security with DLP
WAAS (Web Application and API Security)
questions.explanation: WAAS delivers application-layer protection—OWASP Top 10 coverage, API protection, bot risk management, and DoS protection—deployed through Defenders in front of application workloads. CNNF handles east-west microsegmentation at L3/L4, CIEM analyzes identity entitlements, and data security/DLP scans stored data, none of which inspect L7 web and API traffic.

nodes.title: Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM): Key Ideas
nodes.content: CIEM manages who and what can do what across cloud IAM at scale, focusing on driving identities toward least privilege. In Prisma Cloud, CIEM analyzes net-effective permissions across AWS, Azure, and GCP to surface and remediate excessive or unused entitlements.

flashcards.back: Cloud environments accumulate thousands of identities (users, roles, service accounts, machine identities) with sprawling, over-broad permissions. CIEM continuously inventories and analyzes these entitlements to enforce least privilege and shrink the attack surface created by excessive access.

The actual access an identity ends up with after combining all sources — directly attached policies, group/role memberships, inherited and resource-based policies, and any restrictions. CIEM computes this true effective access rather than reading one policy in isolation, because that's what an attacker could really use.

flashcards.front: What does 'right-sizing' entitlements mean in CIEM?
flashcards.back: Comparing the permissions an identity is granted against the permissions it actually uses, then recommending a tighter policy that keeps only what's needed. This least-privilege right-sizing removes unused and excessive permissions without breaking legitimate workloads.

flashcards.front: Why does Prisma Cloud CIEM work across AWS, Azure, and GCP?
flashcards.back: Each provider has a different IAM model, so risky over-permissioning hides in cloud-specific details. CIEM normalizes entitlements across all three into one view, letting teams detect excessive or unused access and enforce consistent least-privilege policy regardless of which cloud the identity lives in.

questions.q: Security wants to identify and right-size IAM principals that hold far more permissions than they actually use across AWS and Azure. Which Prisma Cloud module computes net effective permissions for this?
choices: Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM / IAM Security)
Cloud Workload Protection runtime defense
The vulnerability management dashboard
Trusted Images
questions.explanation: CIEM, also called IAM Security, calculates net effective permissions across cloud platforms and identity providers, surfacing excessive or unused entitlements so teams can enforce least privilege. Runtime defense protects workload behavior, vulnerability management tracks CVEs, and Trusted Images governs which images may run—none of them compute IAM effective permissions.

questions.q: Prisma Cloud Code Security (formerly Bridgecrew) scans Infrastructure-as-Code such as Terraform and CloudFormation for misconfigurations before deployment. Which open-source engine powers this IaC policy scanning?
choices: Trivy
Checkov
Falco
OPA Gatekeeper
questions.explanation: Code Security is built on Checkov, the open-source static-analysis tool for Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes manifests, ARM, and more). Trivy is Aqua's image/IaC scanner, Falco is a CNCF runtime security project, and OPA Gatekeeper enforces Kubernetes admission policies—none is the engine behind Prisma Cloud Code Security.

questions.q: You must protect containers running on AWS Fargate, where you cannot deploy a host-level Defender or a DaemonSet. Which Prisma Cloud Defender type is used?
choices: Host Defender installed on the underlying EC2 host
Cluster Container Defender deployed as a DaemonSet
App-Embedded Defender embedded into the Fargate task definition
Serverless Defender bundled into a Lambda layer
questions.explanation: Fargate is serverless container compute with no host access, so Prisma Cloud embeds protection directly into the task definition using the App-Embedded (Fargate) Defender. There is no accessible EC2 host for a Host Defender, you cannot run a DaemonSet on Fargate, and the Serverless Defender targets FaaS such as Lambda rather than Fargate containers.

questions.q: In Prisma Cloud CSPM, what must an alert rule reference to determine which cloud accounts its policies are evaluated against and where notifications are sent?
choices: A single IAM role ARN specified per policy
The Defender's runtime model for each workload
A Checkov policy pack imported from the build phase
One or more account groups plus optional notification channels
questions.explanation: An alert rule binds policies to one or more account groups (the scope of cloud accounts evaluated) and optionally to notification or integration channels such as email, Slack, or Amazon SNS for delivery. IAM role ARNs belong to account onboarding, runtime models are part of CWP runtime defense, and Checkov packs belong to Code Security—not CSPM alert routing.
